name: SuperMUC-NG Phase 2 Intel GPU: large prompt replication

nodes.description: Phase 1 (done): jobs/storage documented, L=24 U=5.3 point-defect run verified on Intel GPUs. Phase 2: remove the host work from the QR (the main bottleneck, ~2/3 of a sweep) with unchanged numerics, then cut the remaining sync overhead and fill all 8 PVC tiles, and collect the evidence for a GCS application.
nodes.title: Goal
Read LRZ docs and check on system (sinfo, sacct, module avail)
1-node hello-world GPU job, record wait time and script
Env variables login node vs job
Part 3: L=24 beta=5.3 on Intel GPUs
Audit existing Intel support (NVIDIA-specific vs portable)
Modules and env for ifx, MPI, GPU binding
Small system Intel GPU vs same-compiler ifx CPU
Short L=24 beta=5.3 run vs NVIDIA reference
Local merge into production-mpi and production risk report

nodes.description: Deliverable: numbers that say how much of a sweep is sync/launch overhead, so every later change is judged against them. Criterion: docs/supermuc_large_prompt/SYNC.md with the baseline table.
nodes.title: Part 4: Measure the sync overhead (baseline)

nodes.description: Small Fortran test (in jobs/ or testsuite): empty target region (sync and nowait), target update of 16 bytes D->H and H->D, dispatched zgemm 32x32, alfsh_wait on an empty queue. Report us per op; compare with A30 (BENCHMARKS.md: 12 us empty sync kernel). Run with 2025.1 and 2025.3, 1 rank and 4 ranks per tile with CCS.
nodes.title: Latency microbenchmark on one PVC tile

nodes.description:
Count target regions, target updates, la_* calls and la_sync per sweep (existing upd_cnt/n_flush counters or LIBOMPTARGET_PROFILE=T / unitrace if available). Split by phase: block update, wrap, stabilisation, measurement.
Team session 2026-11-11 (C, LIBOMPTARGET_DEBUG, L=24 one tile): per sweep ~75,000 kernel launches (60,000 gpu_lowrank_mod), ~40,000 dispatched BLAS with interop sync, ~374,000 small H2D copies, ~168,800 first-private arrays; after commit de3f7306: 49,530 launches, 28,544 first-private arrays. See ISSUE_INTEL_VS_A30.md.
nodes.title: Count operations per sweep at L=24

nodes.description:
L=24 (ref_L24 parameters) and L=32: s/sweep per chain and node sweeps/s for 8 ranks (1 per tile) and 32 ranks (CCS). Marginal cost from runs of 1 and 4 sweeps (wall clock, not CPU time). Record xpu-smi per-tile busy.
Team session (C): L=24 one tile 9.0-10.5 s/sweep (in-loop timer; 10.1-14.6 with wall-difference method), phases update 55 %, CGR 17 %, stab 14 %, obs 12 %; L=32 29-32 s. ISSUE_INTEL_VS_A30.md section 3.
nodes.title: Baseline timing with fixed seeds

nodes.description: From the counts and the microbenchmark: sync/launch overhead = ops x cost per op; compare with wall time minus kernel time. Name the top 3 sources of waits by call site (file:line).
nodes.title: Sync-time breakdown

nodes.description:
run_cmp_sng.py/compare.py against the ifx CPU build; acceptance for every later change: Mz=F <= 1e-13 relative, identical configs, ctest 53/53. Script it so one command checks a new binary.
Team session (C): phase2/team/tm_cmp.sh (tol 1e-13 Mz=F) + run_cmp_gg.py (GPU vs GPU bitwise). Controls: eps 1e-12 caught marginally, ALF_GPU_NS=0 not caught at L=12; bitwise GPU-vs-GPU catches 1e-12.
nodes.title: Same-seed check harness ready

nodes.description: Why: VTune (SYNC.md) puts geqrf (oneMKL geqrf_wy_lookahead_hybrid, panel on the host) + ormqr + getrf at ~48 % of the total, ~2/3 of a sweep; block-update syncs are only ~9 %. Owner decision 2026-11-11: QR first; no CholeskyQR2 (changes the algorithm); no STABLOG (its CGR uses host ZGEQP3, not faster). Deliverable: QR_DEVICE.md with timings and accuracy. Criterion: decision whether a device-resident QR is at least 2x faster than oneMKL geqrf with 8 host threads at N=576-1024.
nodes.title: Part 5: QR without host work (same numerics)

nodes.description:
Batch 1 and batch 2 (both flavours) at N=576, 784, 1024: time vs geqrf, and check with VTune or gdb sampling whether any host panel runs. If it is device-only and fast, it is the cheapest solution.
Team session Phase 1 (C, job 560233): geqrf_batch (batch 1) 9.7/28.9 ms vs plain 10.1/28.4 ms at L24/L32 (same hybrid path), getrf_batch 2.6-4x slower. Not host-free in effect; reverted.
nodes.title: oneMKL geqrf_batch: host-free and how fast?

nodes.description: Port reference LAPACK zgeqrf (BSD; oneMKL source is closed and cannot be changed): panel zgeqr2 + zlarft + zlarfb, the level-3 parts via dispatched oneMKL gemm/trmm on the device. Variant A: one kernel per column step. Variant B: one fused kernel per panel (one work-group, barriers inside), nb = 16/32/64. Launch cost is 6-18 us per op (SYNC.md), so variant A costs ~N x few launches; variant B ~N/nb x 5 launches. Standalone test in phase2/, no ALF change yet.
nodes.title: Prototype: device blocked Householder QR (port of LAPACK zgeqrf)

nodes.description: N = 576, 784, 1024 (L = 24, 28, 32): device QR vs oneMKL geqrf with 1 and 8 host threads, 1 rank and 4 ranks per tile (CCS). Accuracy: ||A - QR|| / ||A|| and ||Q^H Q - I|| vs host LAPACK, on random and on column-scaled test matrices.
nodes.title: Benchmark the prototype against geqrf

nodes.description: Cheap lever for the hybrid geqrf meanwhile: 32 ranks x 3 threads vs 16 x 7 vs 8 x 14; record which layout gives the most node sweeps/s.
nodes.title: Host threads per rank and core budget

nodes.description: QR of N_FL = 2 flavours together (geqrf_batch with batch 2, or two concurrent queues) so the host panels of one overlap the device work of the other.
nodes.title: Both flavours at once

nodes.description: Which variant goes into ALF, expected gain per sweep (QR share x speed-up), or why none.
nodes.title: Decision note in QR_DEVICE.md

nodes.description: Deliverable: commits on production-mpi-intel-large-prompt with the device QR behind a run-time switch (default oneMKL until accepted). Criterion: same-seed check vs ifx CPU (Mz=F <= 1e-13, identical configs), Precision Green at CPU level, ctest 53/53, negative control fails, s/sweep L=24/32 in SYNC.md.
nodes.title: Part 6: Device QR in ALF, then the next host parts

nodes.description: Inside the ALF_LA_ONEMKL branch of alf_la_mod.F90; the column-norm pre-pivot already runs on the device (gpu_stab_mod.F90:440). Keep the CUDA path untouched.
nodes.title: Integrate into la_geqrf / la_qrpp (Intel path only)

nodes.description: Check whether oneMKL ormqr has a host part (VTune); if yes, apply Q with the same device zlarfb code.
nodes.title: ormqr and ungqr on the device

nodes.description: Same-seed check, Precision Green, ctest, a planted defect in the QR must fail the check; L=24 and L=32 s/sweep, 8 and 32 ranks.
nodes.title: Verify and time

nodes.description: getrf is also host-assisted (13 ms at N=1024, 3.7 % of the total). After the QR: measure its host part and, if worth it, a device LU the same way.
nodes.title: getrf host share (owner: remember this)

nodes.description: Demoted 2026-11-11: block-update syncs are ~9 % of the total (SYNC.md), max ~10 % gain. Deliverable: best runtime settings and the small code changes that still pay off after Part 6.
nodes.title: Part 7: Sync and launch overhead (lower priority)

nodes.description: CCS 4 ranks per tile (32 per node), N_delay 64 and 128, Nwrap 10 and 20, 3-4 host threads, I_MPI_PIN_DOMAIN=auto, AOT build (short-prompt session: ifx_aot wrapper). Nwrap 20 needs the Precision Green check (max <= 2e-9).
nodes.title: Combine both sessions' settings

nodes.description: First confirm the variable exists (strings on libomptarget.rtl.level0.so, Intel docs). Test sync / async / async_ordered on L=24; same-seed check is mandatory (async may reorder host reads).
nodes.title: LIBOMPTARGET_LEVEL_ZERO_COMMAND_MODE=async_ordered

nodes.description: Immediate command lists (LIBOMPTARGET_LEVEL_ZERO_USE_IMMEDIATE_COMMAND_LIST, SYCL_PI/UR_L0 variants), LIBOMPTARGET_LEVEL_ZERO_MEMORY_POOL, oneAPI 2025.0 vs 2025.1 vs 2025.3. Keep only what repeats (noise +-15 %: repeat twice).
nodes.title: Other runtime knobs, one at a time

nodes.description: Draft (do not send) a service-desk request: NEO 23.43 is from 2023; ask for a newer compute runtime, with the microbenchmark numbers as evidence. The user sends it.
nodes.title: Ask LRZ about the GPU driver

nodes.description: oneMKL dispatch and the SYCL shim already finish before returning, so la_sync/om_sync in blk_begin/blk_end (gpu_lowrank_mod.F90:1205, 1238) and the ensure_* helpers may be no-ops on ALF_LA_ONEMKL. Measure, then skip them there.
nodes.title: Drop redundant waits on the Intel path

nodes.description: need_z/guard_gemm call omp_target_is_present for every array of every BLAS call (alf_la_mod.F90 ~550). Compile them only in a debug build for ONEMKL.
nodes.title: Make the guard checks debug-only

nodes.description: Use !$omp dispatch nowait (or the shim with an in-order sycl::queue) for BLAS, and remove wait_and_throw from the shim LAPACK calls; la_sync stays the only wait before host reads (as on CUDA). Check that target regions and the queue are ordered (test hook ALF_LA_TEST_BREAK_ORDER).
nodes.title: Asynchronous oneMKL calls on an in-order queue

nodes.description: In blk_end/blk_flush: one launch for both flavours (N_FL=2) of k_blk_scale_rows, k_blk_scale_cols and k_sub_flush_gather, or one fused kernel; use om_gemm_batched for the two flush GEMMs of both flavours.
nodes.title: Fuse the per-block kernels

nodes.description: Pack bsd, cbuf, bS_d and nsigma_d uploads into one buffer and one target update; keep the single blocking gbd download.
nodes.title: Bundle the per-block transfers

nodes.description: Update SYNC.md: ops per sweep, s/sweep, node sweeps/s at L=24 and L=32, numerics result.
nodes.title: Re-measure after each change

nodes.description: Deliverable: a layout and code state where every tile is busy all the time and the compute units do useful work. Criterion: xpu-smi busy >= 95 % on all 8 tiles; VTune XVE active reported; node sweeps/s maximised.
nodes.title: Part 8: Fill the GPU (target 100 % busy, high XVE use)

nodes.description: xpu-smi dump per tile (busy %) over a full run, VTune GPU offload (busy %, XVE active/idle) for 1 rank and for 4 ranks per tile with CCS.
nodes.title: Measure utilisation of the best configuration

nodes.description: With cheaper host work per rank, more ranks may fit: CCS 2 vs 4, 2/4/6/8 ranks per tile, 1-4 host threads. Find the throughput optimum.

nodes.description: Use the asynchrony from Part 6 so the next flavour's or block's GPU work runs while the host decides accept/reject (nowait + depend, or two queues).

nodes.description: Plan for one process holding several walkers, each launch serving all of them (extra chain dimension on device arrays). Estimate gain and effort.

nodes.description: After the two design notes, implement the one with the best gain per effort; same verification rules as Part 6.
nodes.title: Implement the better design
